How does a bachelorette night in Old Town Scottsdale actually run?

A bachelorette booking is hours with a chauffeur, not a route we sell you: the published shape is 7 hours, and the clock runs from the first pickup to the last drop-off. 5 party units can hold that window, and stops inside it are free. The service page states the pickup rule plainly: "One pickup address for the whole group and one phone we call — the maid of honor, not the group chat. List every stop on the reservation before the night starts; stops on an hourly charter cost nothing, so there is no reason to leave any of them off." The last clause is the one groups underuse: what costs a night is the stop nobody wrote down. The window itself is the product: "Hourly charters start at four hours. The vehicle stays with your group for the whole booked window, so the clock runs from pickup to the last drop-off, not per stop. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged." A point-to-point transfer instead charges $50 per stop beyond pickup and drop-off — the wrong shape for this night. What the chauffeur handles is what guests least often ask for: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Route, temperature and the wait between stops are the chauffeur's job. Where a commercial vehicle may legally stop is the property's call.

Pink Hummer Limo or a party Sprinter for a bachelorette?

The Pink Hummer Limo is a stretch limousine seating 18, at $295 an hour and $1,180 to start. A party Sprinter seats 13 to 16 at $175 an hour, starting at $700. Per seat at those floors that is $66 against $44, and the gap is what the arrival is worth. A limousine on a Hummer chassis is a lounge you step down into; a party Sprinter is a cabin you step up into, with more standing height and a smaller footprint at a kerb. If the arrival photograph is the point, the Pink Hummer Limo leads the celebration order; if the hours matter more, the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) is the same night for $720 less across 7 hours. The Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter sits between them: 15 seats at $250 an hour, starting at $1,000 and reading $67 a seat. The Party Bus (28 Pax) is the only unit with real floor space, and at $36 a seat the cheapest per head of the 5. Compare that column, not the sticker rate.

What is included on board, and what do the house rules allow?

One page of house rules governs every trip here, whatever the vehicle, and 3 of those rules carry a stated fee. Drinking is allowed for guests 21 and over, eating is not, and smoking or vaping of any kind carries a $1,500 fee that no bachelorette booking waives. What comes with the vehicle: "Bottled water is on board and it is the only complimentary amenity; refreshments, custom signage and anything else are add-ons you choose at checkout." Space is the other limit: "This is a lounge cabin, not a luggage van. Bring what you can hold, and if the night starts or ends at a hotel with everyone’s bags, tell us so we can confirm the fit in writing." Three of those rules carry a fee. "No smoking or vaping of any kind. The smell does not leave, so this one carries a fee." ($1,500). "Keep the drinks in the cups. Minor spills are fine; a can or two on the floor counts as excessive and carries a cleaning fee." ($450). "If someone gets sick in the vehicle, we have to deep clean it, and that carries a cleaning fee. Pace yourselves." ($450). Condition is documented, not argued afterwards. "Before every trip your chauffeur takes a documented set of photos of the interior. They are for our internal records only." "You authorize us to charge the card on file for damage beyond normal use. We will never charge for damage without telling you first, with the photos, so there are no surprises."
